# SEO-049: Emit one absolute self-referencing canonical per indexable page

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Domain | `canonicals` |
| Category | `TECHNICAL_SEO` |
| Minimum level | `LITE` |
| Severity | `HIGH` |
| Impact | `HIGH` |
| Change safety | `REVIEW_REQUIRED` |
| Evidence tier | `A` |
| Confidence | `HIGH` |

## Statement

Each indexable page declares exactly one canonical link whose href is an absolute URL on the production origin and equals the URL that serves the page, with no second canonical element anywhere in the document.

## Rationale

A single unambiguous self-reference tells the engine which address represents this content; a missing declaration leaves the choice to heuristics, and two competing declarations are treated as a conflict the engine resolves on its own.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Derive the value from the resolved route path joined to the configured production origin, emitted once from the layer that owns the document head. Remove any duplicate canonical contributed by a plugin, layout, or CMS field before adding a new one.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Count canonical link elements in the served response for a route sample and record each href alongside the request URL that produced it.
- Evidence: `RENDERED_HTML`, `RAW_HTML`, `ROUTE`
- Automated check: `canonical-self-referencing-absolute`

## Scope

- Search surfaces: `GOOGLE_SEARCH`, `BING_SEARCH`
- Frameworks: `any`
- Caution: none recorded.
